paper.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts

problem_tree.node: Root: Understanding how language models utilize long input contexts
problem_tree.description: This research investigates the performance of language models when processing long contexts, particularly focusing on their ability to access and utilize relevant information effectively.

children.node: RQ1: How does the position of relevant information within long input contexts affect language model performance?
children.description: This question explores the impact of changing the position of relevant information in the input context on the performance of language models in multi-document question answering tasks.

children.task: Evaluate multi-document question answering performance with varying positions of relevant information.
children.protocol_or_setup: Vary the position of the relevant document in the input context.
children.conclusion: Performance is highest when relevant information is at the beginning or end of the context, showing a U-shaped performance curve.

children.node: RQ2: To what extent can language models retrieve information from their input contexts?
children.description: This question investigates the ability of language models to retrieve relevant information from their input contexts using a synthetic key-value retrieval task.

children.task: Conduct a synthetic key-value retrieval task to assess retrieval performance.
children.protocol_or_setup: Vary the position of the key within the JSON object and the number of key-value pairs.
children.conclusion: Models struggle to retrieve information from the middle of the input context, exhibiting a U-shaped performance curve.

children.node: RQ3: What factors contribute to the robustness of language models in utilizing long input contexts?
children.description: This question examines the influence of model architecture, query-aware contextualization, and instruction fine-tuning on the performance of language models with long contexts.

children.task: Analyze the effect of model architecture on performance with long contexts.
children.protocol_or_setup: Compare decoder-only and encoder-decoder models on long input sequences.
children.conclusion: Encoder-decoder models show more robustness to changes in the position of relevant information compared to decoder-only models.

children.task: Evaluate the impact of query-aware contextualization on retrieval tasks.
children.protocol_or_setup: Implement query-aware contextualization in the input format.
children.conclusion: Query-aware contextualization improves performance on key-value retrieval but has minimal effect on multi-document QA.
